- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending down.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (price drops >5% from recent high), model often fails to correct; add 1–2% downward bias in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ true values before projecting.
